E. Pacific Tropical Outlook

NHC issued: 1000 PM PST Sun Nov 8 2026
Eastern East Pacific (EP96):
Recent satellite wind data indicates that a small area of low pressure located more than one hundred miles offshore of Nicaragua and El Salvador has a well-defined circulation and is producing winds of 30-35 mph near its center. However, the associated shower and thunderstorm activity has become less organized near its center. Environmental conditions are forecast to become less favorable for additional development over the next several days as the system moves westward or west-southwestward away from land, and the chances of it becoming a short-lived tropical cyclone are decreasing. Regardless, this system is expected to bring periods of heavy rain to portions of Central America over the next day or so.
